F01.what_it_tests: Select records that meet stated conditions
F01.illustration: Which listed request is both signed and marked urgent?

F02.what_it_tests: Apply an implication from its trigger
F02.illustration: If an active badge grants entry and this badge is active, what follows?

F03.what_it_tests: Reason backward from a missing required condition
F03.illustration: Every approved request needs a valid ticket; can one without a ticket be approved?

F04.what_it_tests: Track combinations such as both, either and exactly one
F04.illustration: Which choice satisfies exactly one of two stated conditions?

F05.what_it_tests: Track all, some, none and overlapping groups
F05.illustration: All teal tokens are marked; no marked token is blank; which relation follows?

F06.illustration: A is taller than B and B than C; how do A and C compare?

F07.what_it_tests: Fit events around order and exclusion rules
F07.illustration: Which timetable puts one meeting before another without overlapping a break?

F08.what_it_tests: Give each item a unique partner while satisfying clues
F08.illustration: Assign three people different desks using location restrictions.

F09.what_it_tests: Count precisely how many statements hold
F09.illustration: Under the supplied facts, how many of six claims are true?

F10.what_it_tests: Find a consistent pattern of truthful and false statements
F10.illustration: Which assignment of honest and dishonest speakers fits their claims?

F11.what_it_tests: Determine whether facts force an answer or contradict one another
F11.illustration: Is a proposed arrangement determined, impossible or still underdetermined?

F12.illustration: A red token starts in box A; several box contents are swapped; where does it end?

F13.what_it_tests: Apply each ordered edit to the current state
F13.illustration: Toggle one flag, swap two values, then conditionally reset another flag.

F14.what_it_tests: Compare starts, ends and overlapping periods
F14.illustration: Which interval overlaps a specified event without containing it?

F15.what_it_tests: Update position or direction from described movement
F15.illustration: Follow successive turns and moves, then identify the final direction.

F16.what_it_tests: Resolve chains of names, roles and references
F16.illustration: Identify the mentor of the colleague named in a nested description.

F17.illustration: An object moves while one observer is absent; where will that observer look?

F18.what_it_tests: Recompute consequences of changing a specified input
F18.illustration: Force a switch off while holding other inputs fixed; which lamp now lights?

F19.what_it_tests: Apply a rule, its exception and stated precedence
F19.illustration: A badge permits entry unless a higher-priority suspension applies.

F20.what_it_tests: Choose an action sequence whose requirements are met
F20.illustration: Obtain a key before opening a locked door, with limited moves available.

F21.what_it_tests: Follow arrows in their permitted direction
F21.illustration: Can node A reach node D through the listed directed links?

F22.what_it_tests: Rank candidates using explicit tie-break rules
F22.illustration: Rank by priority first, then age when priorities tie.

F23.what_it_tests: Find a case that violates a stated rule
F23.illustration: Which listed record disproves the claim that every approved item is signed?

F24.what_it_tests: Select the valid source rather than an outdated conflicting one
F24.illustration: Two records disagree; which controls under the stated authority and date policy?

F25.what_it_tests: Match observed symptoms to explicit fault rules
F25.illustration: Which fault is consistent with the supplied test results?

F26.what_it_tests: Choose the action with the lowest probability-weighted cost, using the supplied likelihoods and costs.
F26.illustration: Which action minimizes the expected cost of a possible delay?

F27.what_it_tests: Decide whether paying for a test before choosing an action reduces the probability-weighted cost enough to cover the test price.
F27.illustration: Should you buy a sensor reading before choosing an action, or is acting without the extra information cheaper overall?
F27.display_name: Is extra information worth its cost?

F28.what_it_tests: Follow the stated worst-case rule when likelihoods are not supplied. Minimize either the largest possible loss or the largest regret (extra loss compared with the best action for each situation), as the question specifies. Do not invent probabilities.
F28.illustration: A route costs 4 in either situation; another costs 1 or 9. With no probabilities and a smallest-worst-case-cost rule, which route should be chosen?

F29.what_it_tests: Choose an action while accounting for the specified choices or payoff-maximizing response of another decision-maker.
F29.illustration: Which first move gives the best result after the other player chooses their own best reply?

F30.what_it_tests: Decide whether overlapping operations and their reported results can fit a permitted one-at-a-time order that respects the specified timing and object rules.
F30.illustration: Two processes read and change the same stored value. Could their reported results fit an allowed one-at-a-time order?

F31.what_it_tests: Check whether changing a protected secret can change an observable result in a way the stated policy forbids.
F31.illustration: If public inputs stay the same, could public output distinguish two secret values that the policy says must remain indistinguishable?
